utterances.text: No. We could not do that at all. We could only admit persons to prison on the basis of a decision of a competent court, and once that court brought the decision of releasing the person, we would do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You referred to different categories of people. You said some people who were convicted by misdemeanors judge and then by those under investigation and -- were they altogether?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAGISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were not. We had three groups of persons deprived of liberty, and we sought to separate -- we didn't seek. We practiced to separate those three groups. Those convicted of misdemeanors were in one section, criminally persecuted -- prosecuted persons were in yet another part. And prisoners of war of Croat ethnicity were in a third section.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that these three groups or persons could not or could intermingle and have mutual contact?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAGISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they could not have mutual contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As the keeper of the central register, did you prepare reports and submit data on inmates and on the status of the central registry to, for instance, the Ministry of Justice and Administration?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAGISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We mainly prepared monthly or annual reports. The annual report being a broader one, encompassing all of the persons staying in the prison, all of the inmates. And indicating on what grounds they were there, and such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: So you say the annual report of the central register operator was a broader one, but where did you get that input? On the basis of what information did you prepare such reports?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAGISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a log. I had a logbook. All of those who would be brought into the district prison in Knin would have their documents stating on what grounds they were being brought there, and I would enter that into the register, their names, the competent court, the issuing authority of the detention order, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were those acts, those documents, decisions of the court indicate the actual criminal offence, the punishment and the other -- and the rest?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAGISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can we please look at Exhibit 908. Do you recognise this document? Can we see it a bit closer up, please.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAGISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report of the central record keeper for 1994, I suppose that's the one we are talking about. I suppose I drafted it although I would have to see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can we look at page 3 in B/C/S, that is the last page of this report. And in B/C/S, the last digits of the ERN number are 6267. That's page 2. We need the one behind that. Page 3. We see the date at the bottom and on the right-hand side the name and signature. Can you read it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAGISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Knin, 31st of December, 1994 and there is my name and signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you are the author of the report?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAGISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: At the top we see it reads like this: "At the district prison in Knin, in the course of 1994, there were -- there were no cases of self-mutilation by inmates. We also note that there were no cases of murder or suicide. And we did not have any cases of escape".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Where are you reading?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, excuse me. That is just above the signature, four or five lines above the signature. It should be the penultimate paragraph, two brief sentences. So the paragraph begins with the words: "At the district prison in Knin, in the course of 1994."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The English is slightly different. Okay, fine.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. I see they say there were "no cases of self-inflicted wounds at the Knin district prison in 1994. Also there were no cases of homicide or suicide". Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you said you had insight into this information.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAGISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Could we say about the district prison in Knin that it was an installation for short-term or long-term detention with a purpose of abuse, torture or even killing of people just on the grounds of their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DRAGISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Certainly not. It was just a regular prison, and there were no cases of the kind you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have almost reached the end of my examination. I have only two or three brief questions left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe just ask them, could you? Do not forget Judge Nosworthy has to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant to continue tomorrow, because I suppose my colleague from the Prosecution will have questions and you too as the Trial Chamber. That was my meaning. I have only two or three questions and I will ask them tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: One very short question. What do you mean by the words "it was a regular prison." Do you know other prisons? Or how come you say -- what is a regular prison, in your eyes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not use the word regular in Serbian. I meant it was a real prison of the only type that usually existed everywhere. It was the only one in Knin municipality. There was another district prison in Glina and a district prison in Beli Manastir. In Glina there was also a correctional facility for convicts. Those were the three district prisons that were in operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no other kind of prison that could possibly exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have come to the end of the day. The matter will stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9 o'clock. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 21st day of September, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
